title: Google developer documentation style guide
supports: Editorial guidelines for developer documentation; the guide calls itself guidelines, not rules; project style comes first, then the guide, then other references. Credited by name; not reproduced

title: Procedures (Google developer documentation style guide)
supports: Numbered steps, an introductory sentence, generally one action per step, location before action, results in a separate paragraph, optional steps marked, one keyboard-accessible method

title: API reference code comments (Google developer documentation style guide)
supports: What to document for every public class and method (parameters, return values, exceptions, permissions), opening verbs, short code samples, deprecation notes that name the replacement

title: Welcome - Microsoft Writing Style Guide
supports: The online guide replaces the Microsoft Manual of Style and covers voice, bias-free and global communication (page updated 15 Oct 2026). Credited by name; not reproduced

title: Writing tips (global communications) - Microsoft Writing Style Guide
supports: Writing for readers whose first language is not English and for machine translation: short sentences, keep 'that' and articles, one word per concept, avoid idioms and modifier stacks

title: Plain language guide series
supports: US federal plain language guidance, successor to PlainLanguage.gov; the Plain Writing Act of 2010 requires public content written for its audience; write, design and test for understanding

title: Writing for understanding
supports: Active voice makes clear who does what; present tense; avoid hidden verbs; shorter words and sections

title: Use clear language (Writing to GOV.UK standards)
supports: Split sentences over 25 words; paragraphs of five sentences or fewer; about 1 in 6 adults in England have very poor literacy; in one study 80% preferred clear English in legal documents; explain specialist terms

title: How to write clearly
publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Translation (Publications Office of the EU)
supports: EU plain-writing guide (2015, available in 24 languages); think about the reader and the purpose; hints rather than rules

title: The Nurnberg Funnel: Designing Minimalist Instruction for Practical Computer Skill (John M. Carroll, 1990)
supports: Bibliographic record (MIT Press, 1990); source of the minimalist instruction ideas summarised in the canon

title: The map (Diátaxis)
supports: Four documentation types (tutorials, how-to guides, reference, explanation) placed on two dimensions: action or knowledge, and acquiring or applying skill

title: Colophon (Diátaxis)
supports: Diátaxis was created by Daniele Procida, with origins in his work at Divio (2014 to 2021); first aimed at software product documentation

title: Docs as Code
supports: Docs as code uses issue trackers, version control, plain-text markup, code review and automated tests; teams can block merges without docs; adoption talks from Google, Microsoft, AWS, GOV.UK GDS and others

title: github/docs: the open-source repo for docs.github.com
supports: GitHub's documentation is written in Markdown in a public repository, accepts outside contributions to content files, and licenses content under CC-BY-4.0

title: About READMEs
supports: What a README usually covers (what, why, how to start, help, maintainers); where GitHub looks for it; content over 500 KiB is truncated; automatic outline from headings

title: OpenAPI Specification (latest: v3.2.1)
supports: OpenAPI 3.2.1 dated 10 September 2026; a language-agnostic description of HTTP APIs used to generate docs, clients, servers and tests; description fields support CommonMark

title: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
supports: Standard machine-readable error format (July 2023, obsoletes RFC 7807): application/problem+json with type, status, title, detail and instance

title: AIP-193: Errors
supports: Error messages should help a technical user fix the problem; stable machine-readable reasons; links to troubleshooting docs; localized messages

title: General Product Safety Regulations 2005 (guidance)
publisher: GOV.UK (Office for Product Safety and Standards)
supports: Great Britain guidance for producers and distributors: consumer products must be safe in normal or reasonably foreseeable use; last updated 13 December 2024

title: Keep a Changelog 1.1.0
supports: Changelogs are for humans; newest first; Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security; an Unreleased section; YYYY-MM-DD dates; state whether Semantic Versioning is followed

title: PEP 257: Docstring Conventions
supports: Docstring conventions: one-line summary in command form, blank line, detail; document arguments, return values, side effects, exceptions and restrictions

title: Documenting Architecture Decisions (Michael Nygard, 15 November 2011)
supports: Architecture decision records: title, context, decision, status, consequences; numbered, kept in the repository, superseded rather than deleted, one or two pages

title: KCS v6 Practices Guide
supports: Knowledge-Centered Service: Solve Loop (capture, structure, reuse, improve) and Evolve Loop (content health, process integration, performance assessment, leadership); v6 released 21 April 2016, PDF updated 7 April 2025

title: F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web: Misunderstood, But Still Relevant (Even on Mobile)
supports: F-pattern scanning when pages lack cues (research 2006, article 2017, reviewed 19 Aug 2026); fixes: key points first, headings that start with information-carrying words, lists, descriptive links

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
supports: W3C Recommendation (12 December 2024 version); 1.1.1 text alternatives (A); 2.4.6 headings and labels (AA); 3.1.5 reading level, lower secondary education (AAA); 3.3.2 labels or instructions (A)

title: General product compliance
supports: Manufacturers draw up instructions and safety information in a language easily understood by consumers; importers and distributors check language requirements for the country of sale (page last checked 13 Jul 2026)

title: Machinery
publisher: European Commission (Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs)
supports: Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027 and clarifies when instructions for use can be supplied in digital form

title: 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey: Developers
supports: 67.8% of respondents to the learning question used technical documentation to learn to code in the past year; for learning AI coding, AI tools 52.5% and technical documentation 42.5%

title: 2025 State of the API Report
supports: Survey of over 5,700 developers, architects and executives: 55% struggle with inconsistent documentation; 41% use AI to generate API documentation; 24% design APIs with AI agents in mind

title: The /llms.txt file
supports: A proposal (first published 3 Sep 2024, modified 10 Aug 2026), not a ratified standard, for a Markdown file at /llms.txt and .md page versions that help AI agents use a site
